analysis.investment_thesis: Capillary Technologies is a money-losing SaaS company dressed in a speculative growth narrative, trading at P/E 420x and P/B 6.97 — roughly 10x my Graham Number of ~₹53 versus a market price of ₹566. Four consecutive years of net losses (2021–2024) disqualify it entirely from my required earnings track record, and the sole profitable year (₹13 Cr net profit in FY2025) is contradicted by deeply negative free cash flow of -₹94 Cr that same year.
key_strengths: Revenue growing at 36.7% CAGR (2021–2025), demonstrating real market demand for its loyalty/CRM SaaS products
Low debt-to-equity of 0.17 with net cash position (₹201 Cr cash vs ₹106 Cr debt) — balance sheet is not a crisis
EBITDA turned positive in FY2025 (₹72 Cr) after years of heavy losses, suggesting operating leverage may be emerging
key_risks: Earnings history is wholly inadequate — net losses of ₹23, ₹101, ₹88, and ₹57 Cr across 2021–2024 fail my minimum 3–5 year positive earnings test
Free cash flow -₹94 Cr in FY2025 despite accounting profit of ₹13 Cr reveals that reported profitability is not yet translating into real cash returns to shareholders
P/B of 6.97 means the market is paying ₹7 for every ₹1 of net assets — at this price, even a modest deterioration in sentiment could destroy 70–80% of market value
red_flags: P/E of 420x — roughly 28x my maximum tolerable P/E of 15; there is zero margin of safety
Graham Number ≈ ₹53 vs current price ₹566 — stock trades at approximately 10x intrinsic value by my calculation
Negative FCF in 4 of the last 5 years (-₹11, -₹10, -₹48, +₹60, -₹94 Cr) — the business has been a consistent cash incinerator
ROE of 2.56% and ROCE of 2.88% are below the risk-free rate — management is destroying capital in real terms
Zero dividend history — shareholders receive no tangible return; all value is speculative price appreciation
analysis.detailed_analysis:
Every quantitative filter I apply condemns this stock. The Graham Number — derived from FY2025 EPS of ~₹1.64 and book value per share of ~₹75 — yields roughly ₹53, against a market price of ₹566. The stock would need to fall approximately 90% merely to reach fair value by my method. The P/B of 6.97 is nearly five times my ceiling of 1.5, and the P/E of 420x is 28 times my maximum of 15. ROE of 2.56% and ROCE of 2.88% confirm that even at the asset level, capital is being deployed with virtually no return. There is no margin of safety anywhere in this price.

The earnings record is equally disqualifying. My discipline requires at minimum three to five consecutive years of positive earnings before I will consider a purchase; Capillary posted losses every single year from 2021 through 2024 (cumulative net loss of ~₹269 Cr). The solitary profitable FY2025 figure of ₹13 Cr is rendered meaningless by a concurrent free cash flow of -₹94 Cr — the business consumed more cash than it earned. Financing cash flows have propped the company up for years; this is the very definition of a speculative enterprise. I am reminded that Mr. Market occasionally offers sound businesses at bargain prices — this is not one of them at any price remotely near the current level.
